usageNotes: Registers a new ACME account with a CA (defaults to Let's Encrypt production) and stores the account credentials in a named config file on the cluster. The `contact` field must be a valid email address that will receive expiry and revocation notices from the CA. If the CA requires External Account Binding (e.g. ZeroSSL, sectigo), supply both `eab-kid` and `eab-hmac-key` together; omitting one will cause registration to fail. You must pass the CA's Terms of Service URL via `tos_url` to indicate acceptance — most CAs will reject registration without it.

examples.summary: Register a default Let's Encrypt account with ToS acceptance

tips: Let's Encrypt staging directory (https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory) is useful for testing; certificates it issues are untrusted but rate limits are much higher.
The `name` field becomes the config file identifier reused when assigning this account to ACME domain entries — use a descriptive name (e.g. 'letsencrypt', 'zerossl') if you manage multiple CAs.
Only one account per name is allowed; attempting to register a duplicate name will return an error — use get_cluster_acme_account_name first to check existence.
EAB credentials are one-time-use secrets provided by the CA dashboard; store them securely before submitting — Proxmox does not echo them back after registration.
